newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major feels growing support on streets.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major feels growing support on streets.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday that the reaction he was getting out on the streets was at odds with opinion polls showing his Conservative Party way behind the opposition Labour Party.
"The opinion polls are just wrong," Major, campaigning for the May 1 election in south-west England, told BBC radio.
"Go out there. It isn't like that in the crowds and it isn't like that on the doorstep."

Major, who defied pollsters to win the 1992 election, said that meeting people face to face was a better indicator of support than the figures produced by statisticians. Opinion poll currently put the Conservatives some 20 points behind Labour.
"If you're actually out there in the midst of a crowd there's an atmosphere. The way people react, the body language, the welcome, the number of people who are there," said Major.
"It's an instinct. The only word for it is feel. Heaven forbid that I ever have to answer for the opinion polls. I can just tell you it doesn't feel like that out there," he said.
